subject.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw publish a manifest-gated, single-slot `MemoryRerankProvider` plugin SDK seam for builtin memory search now?
rationale: The implementation is plausible, but the permanent plugin API shape, exclusive-slot semantics, builtin-only scope, and relationship to broader external-reranker work require maintainer product/API ownership before release.

options.title: Approve Seam After Rebase
options.body: Accept the generic plugin SDK direction, resolve conflicts against current main, and require exact-head rerank/fail-open/API-baseline validation before merge.

options.title: Request API Shape Revision
options.body: Keep the PR open but ask for a different provider selection, manifest declaration, qmd scope, or compatibility story before publishing the contract.

options.title: Pause For External Plugin Direction
options.body: Defer or close this PR if maintainers prefer the concrete external-reranker plugin/config work to own the first shipped path instead of adding a core SDK seam now.

recommendation.title: Approve Seam After Rebase
recommendation.body: Accept the generic plugin SDK direction, resolve conflicts against current main, and require exact-head rerank/fail-open/API-baseline validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about plugin SDK and memory-host contract shape, where recent history shows the strongest ownership signal.
